title: GitHub Agentic Workflows reaches general availability with policy-gated outputs
dek: Markdown-defined agent tasks compile into GitHub Actions and run with read-only defaults, sandboxing and a separate checked-output path.
evidence: Official GitHub GA release and project documentation; customer case study is not controlled evidence
takeaway: Agentic CI separates the ability to propose changes from authority to apply them.

sections.title: Context

bullets.detail: A CI automation that can reason about issues and code may also read untrusted text and propose changes. Ordinary workflow credentials and direct write access make prompt injection consequential.

paragraphs: Why scheduled agents differ: A CI automation that can reason about issues and code may also read untrusted text and propose changes. Ordinary workflow credentials and direct write access make prompt injection consequential.

sections.title: What's new

bullets.detail: GitHub's open-source Agentic Workflows project is generally available. A natural-language Markdown workflow compiles into standard GitHub Actions YAML for tasks such as issue triage, CI diagnosis, documentation and tests.

Agents have read-only permissions by default, a content integrity filter, a sandbox behind Agent Workflow Firewall, validated safe outputs, and a separate threat-detection job before proposed changes are applied.

The release adds support for self-hosted Actions Runner Controller with Docker-in-Docker, Cloud Hypervisor or NVX micro-VM isolation, cross-repository enclaves, model-provider selection and `gh aw forecast` budget estimates.

paragraphs: Declarative compilation: GitHub's open-source Agentic Workflows project is generally available. A natural-language Markdown workflow compiles into standard GitHub Actions YAML for tasks such as issue triage, CI diagnosis, documentation and tests.

Layered execution controls: Agents have read-only permissions by default, a content integrity filter, a sandbox behind Agent Workflow Firewall, validated safe outputs, and a separate threat-detection job before proposed changes are applied.

GA additions: The release adds support for self-hosted Actions Runner Controller with Docker-in-Docker, Cloud Hypervisor or NVX micro-VM isolation, cross-repository enclaves, model-provider selection and `gh aw forecast` budget estimates.

sections.title: Evidence & limitations

bullets.detail: GitHub says Agentic Workflows is generally available on github.com for Free, Team and Enterprise. Using the default Copilot CLI engine requires a Copilot license; alternative agents can be configured.

GitHub quotes one customer's estimated 29 hours saved per week by a lead engineer and a reduction in daily production errors. These are uncontrolled customer observations, not independent causal measurements of the framework.
A firewall and sandbox constrain capabilities, but cannot determine whether a semantically valid patch is correct or whether an approved write is authorized in business context.

sections.title: Key takeaways

bullets.detail: Sandboxing limits agent access. Output validation limits which proposed effects can become repository actions.
A Markdown task expresses intent, but workflow tokens, triggers and output gates determine enforceable authority.

paragraphs: Separate boundaries: Sandboxing limits agent access. Output validation limits which proposed effects can become repository actions.
Prompts are not permissions: A Markdown task expresses intent, but workflow tokens, triggers and output gates determine enforceable authority.
